challengeFindings.title: A consumer who lists the claude.ai connector `Linear` in the `.agents/context.md` `mcp-servers` block gets `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__*` pruned and re-added on every install and upgrade, so `bkit check` exits 1 with drift forever

A list value the current template ships again is still pruned and reported as "retired entries bkit removes" on every run, against the plan's edge case "Entry equals a string the current template ships: never removed or reported"

After a real `bkit install` has already removed a retired grant, the post-install checklist still says "retired entries bkit removes" and "Run bkit upgrade to remove a retired entry", which describes nothing left to do

A later retired-list entry on `permissions.deny` or `permissions.ask` silently deletes a person's own identical deny or ask rule on `bkit upgrade`, so agents run a command the project chose to block or confirm
`bkit upgrade` and `bkit upgrade --dry-run` take back a permission entry while printing only `upgrade (merge): .claude/settings.json`, so the person gets no record of which grant or rule changed

tests.testName: keeps a retired value the mcp-servers block derives and records no drift on the next dry run
does not remove a deny rule named by an injected retired list

challengeFindings.title: A consumer upgrading from bkit v0.4.0-v2.2.3 keeps the Linear connector grants bkit shipped (`mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue`, `save_comment`, `list_issues` and seven more), and the upgrade tells them each is their own edit, so an agent steered by issue text still reads and writes their claude.ai Linear workspace without asking

A consumer upgrading from bkit v0.2.0-v0.3.0 or v4.1.5-v4.10.0 silently keeps shipped grants no current release gives (`mcp__*__save_issue` and `mcp__*__save_comment` on every MCP server, `WebFetch` for `z.ai`, `kimi.com`, `moonshot.ai`, `*.nvidia.com` and `supabase.com`), because the retired list comes from a release survey that missed them
